lots.title: Supply of Double Glazed Units
lots.description: Lot 1 of the Bristol City Council 'Supply of Double Glazed Units and Sheet Glass – DPS' (ProContract reference DN625136 / FTS notice BRISTOLCC001-DN625136-76775102). Providers admitted to Lot 1 are entitled to participate in Call-Off competitions for the supply of double-glazed units across the 48-month DPS term commencing 1 December 2022. The ITT does not enumerate detailed technical specifications for the units within Lot 1 itself; product technical requirements (e.g. BS EN 1279 compliance, dimensions, sealing, spacers) are deferred to per-call-off ITTs and to the separate Appendix 1 – Evaluation Criteria document referenced by the procurement.
requirements: Procurement run under the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 using the Open procedure (§1 SECTION ONE – Procurement Process, 1.1).
DPS contract length: 48 months from anticipated commencement 1 December 2022, no option to extend (§1 SECTION ONE – Proposed Contract, 1.1.–1.2.).
Estimated total contract value (inclusive of options) across both lots: £700,000 (§1 SECTION ONE – Proposed Contract, 1.3).
All bid responses, queries, and clarifications must be submitted via the ProContract e-Tendering System (§2 General 1.2; §2 Submission of Bid; §2 Clarification Questions).
Bids must remain open for acceptance for 180 days from the tender return closing date (§2 Bid Validity, 1.1).
Bids must be unqualified and unconditional; bidders must not propose alternative payment terms, insurance, guarantees, or conditions or risk rejection (§2 General, 1.6).
Bidders must accept the Council's bid documentation without reservation; failure to comply may exclude the bid from further consideration (§2 Preparation of Bid, 1.4).
Provider must comply with the Bribery Act 2010, Fraud Act 2006, Data Protection Act 2018 / GDPR (§2 Bribery Act 2010 & Whistleblowing; §2 Fraud Act 2006; §2 Data Protection (GDPR)).
Provider must pay staff engaged on Council contracts at least the Living Wage Foundation rate (§2 Living Wage Foundation, 1.3).

Suppliers are expected to align with the Council's Climate Emergency targets (carbon-neutral by 2030, scope 1/2/3 GHG measurement) and the Sustainable Procurement Policy; Clean Air Zone charges are borne by the supplier (FOREWORD §1 Climate Change and the Environment Sustainability, 1.1.1–1.1.5).

Pricing must be quoted in pounds sterling (GBP), exclusive of VAT, and must include all costs (collection, design, delivery, labour, materials, transport, plant, fuel, training, monitoring, disposal, software/hardware, third-party charges, etc.) (§3 Pricing, 1.2–1.3).
Submitted prices remain fixed for the duration of the contract (§3 Price Adjustment, 1.1).
Council reserves the right to reject bids that appear abnormally low after a request for explanation (§3 Abnormally Low Tenders, 1.1).

Bid submissions are publicly inaccessible until notification of the successful bidder; total bid price of the successful bidder becomes accessible between notification and contract signature (§2 Freedom of Information Act table).

Consortium bids permitted as either lead-partner consortium or joint-and-several-liability consortium; if any consortium member fails Stage 1 Selection Criteria the whole consortium fails (§2 Collaboration Arrangements / Lead partner consortium / Joint and several liability consortia; §3 Stage 1 Selection Criteria, 1.2).
Sub-contracting permitted but lead provider remains responsible; material changes to sub-contracting arrangements may disqualify the bidder (§2 Sub-contracting, 1.2).
Council may make contact post-deadline only to clarify, confirm Selection Criteria evidence, notify award decisions, or agree commencement (§2 Submission of Bid, 1.7.1–1.7.6).
Winning supplier must submit monitoring information demonstrating commitments are being delivered (§3 Monitoring and Contract Management, 1.1).
Contract documents are located in the attachments tab on ProContract; bidder submissions form part of the successful bidder's Contract Documents (§4 SECTION FOUR: CONTRACT, 1.1–1.2).

evaluation_criteria.summary: Pass/Fail gate. Bidders are assessed against the Selection Criteria in Table A of Appendix 1 – Evaluation Criteria. Failure on any Table A question excludes the bidder from further evaluation. For consortium bids, failure of any member is failure of the whole consortium.

ProContract Reference ID: DN625136

The procurement process will be conducted in accordance with the requirements of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015. Specifically, the Council will be using the Open procedure. Find a Tender Service (FTS) Contract Notice reference number BRISTOLCC001-DN625136-76775102 dated 14/09/2022.
The contract length will be for 48 months, with no option to extend.
The anticipated commencement date is 1 December 2022.
The estimated total value of this contract (inclusive of options) is £700,000.00.
The council intents to split the contract into the following lots:
Lot 1 - Supply of Double Glazed Units
Lot 2 - Supply of Sheet Glass
The bid is an unconditional offer and should remain open for acceptance for a period of 180 days from the tender return closing date.
Bid & clarification process opens | 14/09/2022
Closing date and time for receipt by the Council of completed bidder responses via the ProContract tendering system. | 12:00hrs Noon 14/102022 Local Time
Commencement date of contract. | 01/12/2022

Bidders will be assessed against the Selection Criteria as set out in Table A of Appendix 1: Evaluation Criteria. Should a bidder not satisfactorily confirm any of the questions in Table A they will not be considered for further evaluation.

Call Off above £25k – Will be 60% - 80% Price and Quality 0% - 20% and Social Value 20%
All rates and prices must be quoted in pounds sterling (GBP).
VAT should not be included in the bid rates and prices.

The minimum marks for a lump sum price will be zero. Therefore, if a bidder submitted lump sum price that is over 100% higher than the lowest submitted lump sum price this bidder will receive a score of zero for that section of the overall price award criteria.
The proposed prices submitted will remain for the duration in accordance with the contract.
Bristol City Council shall require bidders to explain the price or costs proposed in the tender bid where tenders appear to be abnormally low
It is important that bidder's demonstrate relevant experience when answering any 'Quality Commitment Questions'.
